title: add-invocation-shadow-profiles-and-causal-cost-alerts
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Introduce invocation shadow profiles and causalized token-cost alerting. Provides per-tenant retrospective scoring to reduce noisy alerts and surface true regressions. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: We see recurring small-cost spikes that produce noisy SLO alerts despite being semantically benign. Root cause is often downstream model switching or short-lived prompt-shape changes that current alerting attributes to tenants incorrectly. This PR introduces 'invocation shadow profiles' that capture compact summaries of invocation execution shape (prefix length, kv-cache hit ratio estimate, model-variant fingerprint) and a causalized alerting layer that attributes cost/latency drift to the most likely driver rather than the tenant by default. Summary of changes: added shadow profile generator in the serving runtime, introduced a lightweight causal attribution scorer that runs in the observability service, added a new dashboard and alert rule templates, and wired end-to-end tests and benchmarks. Commits (high-level): 1) Add shadow profile proto and serializer; 2) Instrument runtime to emit shadow-profile sidecar for sampled invocations; 3) Build causal attribution service with noise-aware priors and event windowing; 4) Update observability ingestion pipeline to join shadow profiles and metrics; 5) Add dashboard panels and new alerting rules; 6) Tests and infra: add unit tests for scorer, integration test using replaybench, add e2e smoke. Files changed (high level): src/runtime/shadow_profile.rs added summary serializer and sampling knobs; src/observe/attribution/scorer.py added causal scoring model and CI-configured thresholds; observability/ingest/pipeline.go updated to perform 1:1 join on sampled invocation ids; dashboards/causal-cost-explorer.json new Grafana panels showing per-model and per-tenant causal attribution; alerts/retrospective-cost-alerts.yaml new templated alert; tests/replaybench/shadow_capture.yaml test replay gestures. Runtime knobs: sampling_ratio default 0.002 (configurable per-tenant), max_profile_size 512 bytes, and a privacy-safe hashing pipeline for model and prompt fingerprints. Review conversation summary: Ethan requested deterministic sampling for integration tests and tighter defaults on retention; author replied that tests now inject deterministic seed and retention is capped to 7 days for shadow-profile raw payloads; Priya asked for clarification on attribution priors and whether they bias against recent model rollouts; author added a linear-decay prior and documented fallback to tenant-anchored alerts in low-confidence cases; Marcus requested perf microbenchmarks for emit overhead, author added a benchmark showing median 28us extra per-invocation at 8k seq and 99th 120us under synthetic load. Comments and change requests: - make sampling_ratio configurable via tenant flags (addressed) - add opt-out for enterprise private installs (addressed, KMS key gating documented) - confirm no sensitive prompt text is persisted (addressed, only 64-bit hashed shape signatures stored). Approvals: Ethan approved after second iteration, Priya approved, Marcus approved with no further changes. CI: initial run had one flaky test in replaybench, rerun passed; lint and type checks pass; integration e2e in staging passed. Canary notes: deployed to staging for 48 hours, observed 43% reduction in low-confidence alerts on a noisy customer and no regressions in throughput. Rollout plan: staged rollout by tenant percentage: 0%, 5%, 25%, 100% with metrics validation gates at each step; automatic mute to tenant-anchored alerts if attribution confidence < 0.6 for more than 10 minutes. Backwards compatibility: shadow profiles are emitted only when sampling is enabled and join keys are optional; ingestion side can ignore new fields. Operational notes: dashboard includes a causal attribution heatmap, per-model impact table, and a retrospective alert queue that surfaces suspected misattributions for operator review. Migration: no customer data migration required. Post-merge actions: 1) coordinate with SRE to create alerting playbook entries, 2) add retention policy to tenant docs and compliance, 3) schedule a 1-hour runbook review with support. Related work and references: builds on ENG-7029 (prefetch tracing) and ENG-7182 (invocation coalescing); relates to SUP-1193 investigating noisy alerts for tenant X. Why unique: unlike previous token-level attributions this PR attaches compact execution fingerprints and applies a lightweight causal model that can retroactively re-attribute alerts and mute noisy signals, enabling quieter SLOs without losing signal for true regressions.
